feedback: D1 is a clean but incomplete catalogue. You caught seven of the ten findings and every one you listed carries the right class and CWE with a quoted line: SQLi A03/CWE-89 at login.php 64-67, unsalted MD5 A02/CWE-916 at line 66, JWT alg:none A07/CWE-347 at 48-50, the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 A02/CWE-798 at 30/38, XXE A05/CWE-611, the stored XSS A03/CWE-79 at 02:18:47, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite A05/CWE-614. You also nailed the decoy, naming hash_equals at 51-54 and proving it safe because it is constant-time while pointing out that alg:none and the hardcoded secret defeat the scheme anyway, which is exactly the right verdict. What costs you is three missing findings: no token expiry CWE-613 around lines 74-75, path traversal CWE-22 from the files/?path=/etc/passwd capture at 02:24:02, and the open redirect CWE-601 from ?next= at 02:21:13. Your access-control coverage is thin because cookie flags are the only one of those three you logged. D2 is solid in shape but compressed. You reconciled the SQLi at 02:15:31 and the 312-row enumeration at 02:16:04 with verbatim payloads, but you collapsed the kill chain into four hops and dropped the stored XSS hop and the open redirect hop, so the in-order reconstruction is only about half present. Your CVSS work is the weak spot: you scored SQLi as S:C giving 9.3, but the login bypass itself does not change scope, so SQLi should be AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, and the scope change actually belongs to the forged super_admin token reaching the shared /api/v1/internal service, which you did not surface as the senior insight. Your impact of 312 customers and roughly 63 million naira with the BoltCash six week window is good, but state the assumption behind the naira figure rather than presenting it as a flat total. D3 is your strongest deliverable. The executive summary is jargon-free and lands on the customers-and-naira headline, your findings are tied to evidence, you stated the disproved decoy correctly, you identified F1 as the earliest break with the line that closing it removes the precondition every other hop depended on, you ranked remediation by effort with hour estimates rather than by CVSS, and your two detection stopgaps name exact fields and false-positive rates, the alg:none header check and the SQLi pattern alert. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice and anchors to your findings, and you cite ISC2 canons, but you reference them loosely rather than making a numbered canon load-bearing, and you name the NDPA 2023 but cite no section, so you lose that row entirely. I looked for a way to round D4 up and the evidence did not support it. The single most important fix is to cite NDPA 2023 section 40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification and section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects, and to correct the SQLi CVSS scope to S:U.
